title: A deep learning approach to characterize 2019 coronavirus disease (COVID-19) pneumonia in chest CT images

sections.title: 研究问题
sections.text:

【Objectives · abstract-1-1】To utilize a deep learning model for automatic detection of abnormalities in chest CT images from COVID-19 patients and compare its quantitative determination performance with radiological residents.

evidence.text: To utilize a deep learning model for automatic detection of abnormalities in chest CT images from COVID-19 patients and compare its quantitative determination performance with radiological residents.

sections.title: 研究方法
sections.text:
《A deep learning approach to characterize 2019 coronavirus disease (COVID-19) pneumonia in chest CT images》：方法与研究设计的原文依据。

【Methods · abstract-2-1】A deep learning algorithm consisted of lesion detection, segmentation, and location was trained and validated in 14,435 participants with chest CT images and definite pathogen diagnosis. The algorithm was tested in a non-overlapping dataset of 96 confirmed COVID-19 patients in three hospitals across China during the outbreak. Quantitative detection performance of the model was compared with three radiological residents with two experienced radiologists' reading reports as reference standard by assessing the accuracy, sensitivity, specificity, and F1 score.

【Objectives · abstract-1-1】To utilize a deep learning model for automatic detection of abnormalities in chest CT images from COVID-19 patients and compare its quantitative determination performance with radiological residents.

sections.title: 主要结果
sections.text:
《A deep learning approach to characterize 2019 coronavirus disease (COVID-19) pneumonia in chest CT images》：结果的原文依据；数值与适用人群以引文为准。

【Results · abstract-3-1】Of 96 patients, 88 had pneumonia lesions on CT images and 8 had no abnormities on CT images. For per-patient basis, the algorithm showed superior sensitivity of 1.00 (95% confidence interval (CI) 0.95, 1.00) and F1 score of 0.97 in detecting lesions from CT images of COVID-19 pneumonia patients. While for per-lung lobe basis, the algorithm achieved a sensitivity of 0.96 (95% CI 0.94, 0.98) and a slightly inferior F1 score of 0.86. The median volume of lesions calculated by algorithm was 40.10 cm3. An average running speed of 20.3 s ± 5.8 per case demonstrated the algorithm was much faster than the residents in assessing CT images (all p < 0.017). The deep learning algorithm can also assist radiologists make quicker diagnosis (all p < 0.0001) with superior diagnostic performance.

【Conclusions · abstract-4-1】The algorithm showed excellent performance in detecting COVID-19 pneumonia on chest CT images compared with resident radiologists.
